intro: When it comes to the biggest hotel in central Yasothon, JP Emerald Hotel is usually the first name that comes to mind · It's a 119-room, 3-star hotel on Prapa Road in the Nai Mueang subdistrict, open since 1997 and given a major renovation in 2016 · Its strengths are spacious rooms, ample free parking and meeting/banquet halls for weddings and seminars · The location is a walk from the Ban Singha Tha old town, near Wat Maha That, the Yasothon city museum and the town market · From approx. ฿700/night · Real guest reviews agree the rooms are spacious, the staff helpful and the location handy, though the building is starting to show its age, as older Thai hotels tend to.

body.html: JP Emerald Hotel is a 119-room, 3-star hotel in central Yasothon, on Prapa Road in the Nai Mueang subdistrict · It's a large building that opened in 1997 and went through a major renovation in 2016 · With its many rooms and generous common areas, it has long been the hotel locals pick for weddings, banquets and seminars · Rooms range from Superior to Deluxe in double and twin layouts, suiting solo travellers, couples, families and groups alike.

What guests consistently praise is that the rooms are spacious for the price, clean and quiet · Every room has air conditioning, a refrigerator, an LCD TV, a soaking tub and free Wi-Fi · Many reviews note the renovated rooms look tidy, with new floors and fresh paint, functional and a good fit for a few hundred baht in central Yasothon · There's an on-site restaurant, plus a bar, a billiards room and a massage room for nights when you'd rather stay in · The hotel also has ample free parking, a real advantage of a big property like this — ideal for self-drivers and groups arriving in several cars.
"The room was very spacious, clean and quiet, and the staff were helpful · it's in the centre, walkable to Ban Singha Tha, parking is generous — at a few hundred baht it's good value."

Location is another strong point (7.5 for location on Trip.com) · The hotel is right in central Yasothon, a walk from the Ban Singha Tha old town — the row of old wooden shophouses that's the town's signature spot — and close to Wat Maha That and the Yasothon city museum · Eateries, cafés, convenience stores and the town market surround the hotel, so food is easy to find day and night · It's near the Chi River and the government district, suiting tourists, official-business visitors and anyone stopping over on an Isan road trip.

To be straight with you, per real guest reviews: the most frequently mentioned point is that the building is showing its age, as long-running hotels do — some corners, corridors and the lobby look older than the renovated rooms · A few reviews mention rooms where certain fittings feel dated, such as older tubs or fixtures, thinning towels, or a musty smell in rooms that aren't used often · The other thing to know is that when the hotel hosts a wedding or banquet, it can get noisy and busy, especially in rooms near the banquet hall.

In short: if you want a hotel in central Yasothon with spacious rooms, generous free parking, walkable to Ban Singha Tha, at a few hundred baht, and you don't mind a building that's showing some age — JP Emerald Hotel is a fitting choice · The 7.4 from 16 Trip.com reviews (location 7.5, service 7.4) captures it well: spacious rooms, good staff, handy location, in exchange for the building's age · It suits visitors exploring the old town, hosting an event, on official business, or stopping over for a night on an Isan trip.

A tip from following the reviews here: if room condition matters, ask for a renovated Deluxe room and one away from the banquet hall, especially if you book over a weekend when weddings are common · Test the soaking tub, hot water and air conditioning before you unpack, and ask to move rooms if it's not right — the hotel has plenty of rooms to spare.

honestSummary: JP Emerald Hotel is the best pick for travellers who want a large hotel in central Yasothon — spacious rooms, free parking, walkable to Ban Singha Tha, at a few hundred baht — long-running but with renovated rooms, an on-site restaurant and a banquet hall, good for both staying and hosting events · You just have to accept that the building shows its age, some corners look worn, and it can get busy when there's a banquet.
honestChecks: If you're particular about a fresh building and rooms — the hotel has been open since 1997, so the building and common areas are dated and some in-room fittings are old → ask for a renovated Deluxe room and check the room condition on arrival.
If you want complete quiet — weekends often bring weddings or banquets, which can be noisy and busy → ask for a room on a higher floor away from the banquet hall.
If you expect a pool or full gym — there's no swimming pool; the focus is rooms, a restaurant and a banquet hall → if you want a pool, consider a newer hotel in town.

faq.q: Where is JP Emerald Hotel in Yasothon, and what's nearby?
faq.a: JP Emerald Hotel is at 36 Prapa Road, Nai Mueang subdistrict, in central Yasothon · It's within walking distance of the Ban Singha Tha old town and the town market · It's about a 3-5 minute drive from Wat Maha That and the Yasothon city museum · Eateries, cafés and convenience stores surround the hotel, so food is easy to find.

faq.q: How much does JP Emerald Hotel cost, and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. ฿700/night for a Superior Double · Superior Twin, Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin rooms run about ฿750-฿950 · Prices vary by room type and season, so compare Agoda, Booking and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Is JP Emerald Hotel old, and what condition are the rooms in?
faq.a: The hotel opened in 1997 and was given a major renovation in 2016 · Renovated rooms have new floors and fresh paint and look tidy, but the building and some common areas still look dated, as older hotels do · We'd suggest asking for a renovated Deluxe room and checking the room condition on arrival.

faq.q: Who is JP Emerald Hotel best for?
faq.a: It's best for travellers who want a large hotel in central Yasothon with spacious rooms, free parking, walkable to Ban Singha Tha, at a few hundred baht · It suits families, groups, self-drivers, and anyone hosting a wedding or seminar in town.

faq.q: Does JP Emerald Hotel have a banquet hall and parking?
faq.a: Yes to both · The hotel has meeting rooms and a banquet hall for weddings and seminars, plus ample free parking · Note that it can get noisy and busy when there's a banquet, so if you want quiet, ask for a room away from the banquet hall.

faq.q: Does JP Emerald Hotel have a swimming pool?
faq.a: No, there's no swimming pool · The hotel focuses on rooms, a restaurant, a bar, a billiards room, a massage room and a banquet hall · If you want a hotel with a pool in Yasothon, consider a newer property in this review series.
